newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Rep Bonior arrested in newspaper protest.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Rep Bonior arrested in newspaper protest.

text.p: The second-ranking Democrat in the U.S. House of Representatives, David Bonior, was arrested Friday as part of a protest to support locked-out Detroit News and Free Press workers.

Bonior, the house minority whip who represents blue-collar Macomb County, Mich., was one of six local labour, religious and political leaders who entered the Detroit News building to demand that the newspapers resume contract bargaining and rehire thousands of former striking workers.

The protest came on the eve of the second anniversary of the divisive strike by about 2,500 workers, which began July 13, 1995 and ended when their six unions made an unconditional offer to return to work Feb. 14.

The newspapers and their joint operating agency, Detroit Newspapers, at the time said they would continue to operate with replacement workers and only rehire former strikers as jobs became available. The agency has said it has extended offers to 385 people and has 1,100 on a preferential hiring list.
The six newspaper unions maintain that up to 2,000 workers should be rehired, including 230 who were fired during the strike.

"Our community has been torn apart by this strike," Bonior said in a statement. "It's time for the News and the Free Press -- who are guilty of breaking the law -- to do the right thing and put these locked out workers back on the job."
A National Labour Relations Board administrative law judge in June declared that the strike resulted from unfair labour practices by Detroit Newspapers and ordered them to rehire the former strikers.
The NLRB has asked a U.S. District Court Judge to issue an injunction forcing the newspapers to do so. A hearing on the issue is scheduled for July 31.
Detroit Newspapers spokeswoman Susie Ellwood said Bonior and the others met with News editorial page editor Tom Bray, to discuss issues related to the strike.
When that meeting ended they demanded a meeting with the newspaper's publisher and a top Gannett Co. executive. They refused to leave, so company officials called Detroit police, she said.
"This is not the kind of thing that's going to be very effective at helping us reach a resolution," Ellwood said. "That's going to happen at the bargaining table."
Brad Markell, a United Auto Workers member who was one of the six arrested, said they were all ticketed for trespassing, which carries a $50 fine.
More protests were scheduled for Sunday, the strike's second anniversary.
